reason: The cited evidence shows that Fe20Co20Ni20Mn20Cu20 can form a protective oxide layer and that chloride ions cause localized corrosion, but it provides no data on wear-induced film disruption, rapid oxide reformation kinetics, or the dynamic balance mechanism central to the hypothesis.
premises: Wear disrupts a self-forming passive oxide layer on HEAs, exposing fresh metal and accelerating corrosion.
High configurational entropy in HEAs promotes rapid oxide regeneration that partially restores protection.
The coupled response is dominated by the dynamic balance between oxide removal and reformation.
The Fe20Co20Ni20Mn20Cu20 HEA forms a uniform, self-assembled passive oxide layer.
Chloride ions cause localized pitting/crevice corrosion at sites where the passive film is compromised.
